gaps.sentence: He was so badly ___ in the fall that he needed an operation.
gaps.explanation: badly hurt is the standard collocation meaning seriously injured.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ a diary since she was twelve.
gaps.explanation: keep a diary is the fixed collocation for writing in one regularly.

gaps.sentence: I'd like to ___ a suggestion, if I may.
gaps.explanation: make a suggestion is the fixed collocation; 'say a suggestion' is not used.

gaps.sentence: The storm ___ a lot of damage to the roof.
gaps.explanation: do damage to something is the collocation; past tense 'did' is needed here.

gaps.sentence: Her talk really ___ home the urgency of the situation.
gaps.explanation: 'Drive something home' = make it fully understood.

gaps.sentence: The two sides struggled to ___ an agreement before the deadline.
Make sure you are fully ___ of the terms before you sign.
gaps.explanation: fully aware of something is the fixed collocation meaning knowing completely.
